facts.fact: Campaigns spent $11.1 billion on political advertising in the 2024 election cycle, per AdImpact (2024).
facts.quote: Campaigns spent $11.1 billion on political advertising, the most expensive election in U.S. history

facts.fact: AdImpact via OpenSecrets (2026) projects the 2026 midterms to top $10.8 billion in political ad spending, over 20% higher than the 2022 cycle.
facts.quote: the 2026 midterms are projected to top $10.8 billion, over 20% higher than the 2022 cycle

facts.fact: In 2024, campaigns spent $2.3 billion on connected TV (CTV), which AdImpact via NBC News says was 21% of all political ad spend.
facts.quote: In 2024, campaigns spent $2.3 billion on CTV alone, making up 21% of all political ad spend

facts.fact: Roku (2024) reports that one in three potential voters who watch local news now watch through streaming only.
facts.unit: % of potential voters who watch local news
facts.quote: One in three potential voters who watch local news now watch through streaming only

facts.fact: Experian (2024) reports that 63% more baby boomer viewers and 45% more Gen X viewers cut the cord in 2023 compared to 2022.
facts.unit: % more viewers cutting the cord, 2023 vs 2022
facts.quote: 63% more baby boomers and 45% more Gen X viewers cut the cord in 2023 compared to 2022

facts.fact: Madhive (2024) reports CTV ad completion rates between 90% and 98%.
facts.quote: CTV ads achieve completion rates between 90% and 98%

facts.fact: Jamloop (2024) reports campaigns using CTV alongside traditional TV achieved a 32% increase in total reach compared to traditional TV alone.
facts.quote: Campaigns using CTV alongside traditional TV achieved a 32% increase in total reach

facts.fact: Effectv/Comcast (2022) reports that 51% of frequent voter households reached by streaming were incremental, meaning broadcast TV would not have reached them.
facts.quote: 51% of frequent voter households reached by streaming were incremental

facts.fact: The page recommends a budget of $300 to $1,000 per month to create meaningful reach in a local race district.
facts.quote: Budget: $300-$1,000/month can create meaningful reach in a local district

facts.fact: The page recommends a budget of $1,000 to $5,000 per month for competitive state legislative races.
facts.quote: Budget: $1,000-$5,000/month for competitive races

facts.fact: The page recommends a budget of $5,000 to $25,000 per month for competitive congressional races.
facts.quote: Budget: $5,000-$25,000/month for competitive races

facts.fact: For state legislative races, the page recommends increasing ad frequency in the final 4 to 6 weeks before the election.
facts.quote: Increase frequency in the final 4-6 weeks before the election

facts.fact: For local races, the page recommends focusing on likely voters, defined as people who voted in the last 2-3 similar elections.
facts.quote: Focus on likely voters (people who voted in the last 2-3 similar elections)

facts.fact: In the vendor's political ad timing table, the Name ID phase runs 6-12 months before the election and is allocated 15-20% of the budget.
facts.quote: | Name ID | 6-12 months out | Build name recognition | 15-20% |

facts.fact: In the vendor's political ad timing table, the Issue framing phase runs 3-6 months before the election and is allocated 20-25% of the budget.
facts.quote: | Issue framing | 3-6 months out | Connect your name to key issues | 20-25% |

facts.fact: In the vendor's political ad timing table, the Persuasion phase runs 6-12 weeks before the election and is allocated 25-30% of the budget.
facts.quote: | Persuasion | 6-12 weeks out | Make the case for your candidacy | 25-30% |

facts.fact: In the vendor's political ad timing table, the GOTV phase runs in the final 2-3 weeks and is allocated 25-35% of the budget.
facts.quote: | GOTV | Final 2-3 weeks | Drive turnout among supporters | 25-35% |

facts.fact: According to AdImpact (2024), 51% of total political ad spending in 2024 occurred in the final eight weeks before election day.
facts.quote: 51% of total political ad spending in 2024 occurred in the final eight weeks before election day

facts.fact: The vendor says campaigns can launch political CTV ads for as little as $30 a day.
facts.quote: launch for as little as $30 a day

facts.fact: The vendor recommends that campaigns start with $300-$500 per month to test messaging before scaling as the election approaches.
facts.quote: Start with $300-$500/month to test messaging, then scale as the election approaches

facts.fact: The vendor states that local campaigns such as city council or school board races can run meaningful CTV campaigns for $300 to $1,000 per month.
facts.quote: Local campaigns (city council, school board) can run meaningful CTV campaigns for $300 to $1,000 per month.

facts.fact: The vendor states that competitive state legislative races typically need $1,000 to $5,000 monthly for CTV advertising.
facts.quote: State legislative races typically need $1,000 to $5,000 monthly for competitive districts.

facts.fact: The vendor states that congressional campaigns should plan for $5,000 to $25,000 per month on CTV advertising.
facts.quote: Congressional campaigns should plan for $5,000 to $25,000 per month.

facts.fact: The page projects that the 2026 midterms will see $10.8 billion in total political ad spending.
facts.quote: The 2026 midterms are projected to see $10.8 billion in total political ad spending

facts.fact: The vendor claims that CTV can reduce wasted impressions by 70-80% for a state legislative race compared to broadcast TV.
facts.quote: For a state legislative race, CTV can reduce wasted impressions by 70-80% compared to broadcast.

facts.fact: The vendor states that a professional political ad can be created in about two minutes on its platform.
facts.quote: You can create a professional ad in about two minutes

facts.fact: The page states that political ads on CTV must include a 'Paid for by' disclosure.
facts.quote: All political ads must include a "Paid for by" disclosure

facts.fact: The page states that CTV platforms are not subject to the broadcast 'lowest unit rate' rules that apply during election windows.
facts.quote: CTV platforms are not subject to the same "lowest unit rate" rules that apply to broadcast stations during election windows

facts.fact: The page states that CTV targeting can reach voters at the ZIP code level, and combined with voter file matching can target specific registered voters by household.
facts.quote: CTV targeting can reach voters at the ZIP code level, and when combined with voter file matching, can target specific registered voters by household.
